Smart India Hackathon 2026

Smart India Hackathon is a nationwide innovation initiative that challenges students to solve real problems with practical, scalable technology. Team AQUASTRIP competes in the Hardware category under the Clean & Green Technology theme.

The problem

Leaks in water distribution networks waste treated water, raise pumping costs, cut service levels and let pollutants in at the leak point. Commercial loggers cost ₹30,000 or more each, which rules them out for rural and small-town schemes under the Jal Jeevan Mission.

Our solution

AquaEar is a solar-assisted node that senses pipe vibration and pressure, runs a small TinyML model on the device, and reports over LoRa. It works in two tiers, so costly hardware goes only where a leak is suspected.

Problem statement 26254

Development of Indigenous Leak Detection Sensor Systems for Operation & Maintenance of Water Supply Pipelines.

Organisation

Ministry of Jal Shakti, National Jal Jeevan Mission, Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation. Team name: AQUASTRIP.

Proposed solution

Triage the zone first, then pinpoint the leak with two clamped nodes.

Tiered detection

Level 1 flags a zone from night-time minimum flow, or from a scheduled low-demand acoustic survey where meters are missing. Level 2 pinpoints the leak with nodes on valves and hydrants.

Edge AI

A TinyML model on the node labels the signal as leak, no leak or pump noise, which saves power and cuts false alarms.

Dual-method location

Acoustic cross-correlation finds every leak. Negative pressure wave analysis gives an independent check for bursts.

Rural-ready

Solar power and LoRa mean the nodes need no grid or internet. One gateway per zone links to the cloud over 4G.

What sets it apart

Retrofit-friendly

Clamp-on sensing at existing valves and hydrants, with no pipe cutting. Pressure uses the existing hydrant or air-valve port.

Fully indigenous

Indigenous design, firmware, TinyML model, assembly and enclosure, aligned with Make in India. Core ICs are imported.

Added value

An indicative loss in litres per day and a repair priority score help O&M teams plan work.

How AquaEar works

From solar cell to dashboard, with a pressure trigger for bursts.

  1. Solar panel
  2. Li-ion battery and charge controller
  3. Power regulation
  4. ESP32 / STM32 reads ADXL, pressure and GPS
  5. TinyML classifies the signal
  6. LoRa alert to gateway
  7. Cross-correlation finds the leak
  8. 4G to MQTT, dashboard and SMS

Localization

L = (D − v × Δt) / 2

After an alert, the gateway asks the alerting node and its neighbour for a 1-second snippet, then cross-correlates the two to get Δt. D is the node spacing and v is the wave speed, calibrated on site with a tap at a known position. Nodes re-sync to the GPS PPS signal before each window.

Detection

Leak noise sits below about 500 Hz in plastic pipes and up to about 1.5 kHz in metal ones, so the band-pass filter is set per pipe type. Short checks every 15 to 30 minutes during supply hours give near-real-time alerts, and a longer survey runs in a low-demand window. Pressure is watched continuously at low power.

Hardware (per node)

  • ESP32 / STM32 low-power MCU
  • ADXL345 / ADXL355 MEMS accelerometer
  • 0–10 bar pressure transducer
  • LoRa module (SX1278)
  • GPS module with PPS output and TCXO RTC
  • Li-ion battery and small solar panel
  • Waterproof enclosure with clamp or magnet mount
  • One LoRa gateway with 4G / GSM per zone

Software

  • Embedded C/C++ (Arduino / ESP-IDF)
  • TensorFlow Lite Micro (TinyML)
  • Python with NumPy / SciPy for cross-correlation
  • MQTT broker
  • Flask / Node.js backend and REST API
  • Leaflet map dashboard
  • SMS / WhatsApp alerts
  • MQTT / REST / Modbus export to SCADA

Buildable today, affordable tomorrow

Technical feasibility

  • MCU, accelerometer, pressure sensor, GPS, LoRa and solar power fit one low-power node.
  • About ₹2,300 to ₹5,900 per node, against ₹30,000 or more for commercial loggers.
  • Pinpointing needs at least two nodes per pipe section.

Operational feasibility

  • Duty-cycled sensing keeps the battery going between solar top-ups.
  • Alerts reach the pump operator by SMS or WhatsApp.
  • Data exports to existing SCADA through MQTT, REST or Modbus.

Assumptions we plan for

  • Leak noise fades fast in PVC and HDPE, so range is tens of metres and spacing is set per material.
  • Intermittent supply: surveys run inside supply hours.
  • Litres per day is an estimate, not a measurement.

Why it matters

Social impact

  • Early detection and accurate location of leaks.
  • Faster repairs and less non-revenue water.
  • More reliable water service for villages and small towns.

Benefits

  • Data-driven maintenance priorities for O&M teams.
  • Solar and LoRa remove grid and internet needs at the nodes.
  • Scales to village-level deployment at a fraction of logger cost.

SWOT analysis

Strength

Two-tier design keeps cost low and still pinpoints leaks to within metres.

Weakness

Plastic pipes damp leak noise, which limits the distance between nodes.

Opportunity

Can scale across Jal Jeevan Mission schemes as a low-cost logger alternative.

Threat

Imported core ICs can face supply delays and price swings.

Future vision

Better leak sizing

Use flow data from more zones to turn severity classes into measured litres per day.

Smarter model

Fine-tune the TinyML model on more pipe materials and field recordings.

Wider network

Add more nodes per zone and link zones into one district-level view.
